clues.text: This city sits on the south coast of its land, where the shore meets a wide gulf of the Atlantic Ocean. Sandy beaches line its edge.
clues.narrowing: Puts the player on a south coast, on a gulf of the Atlantic Ocean.

source.quote: is the capital and largest city of Ghana, located on the southern coast at the Gulf of Guinea, which is part of the Atlantic Ocean

clues.text: The air here stays warm all year, and the rains come and go with the seasons. Its climate is drier than the wet coast towns near it.
clues.narrowing: Rules out cold and ever-wet coasts; keeps a warm coast city with a drier climate.

source.quote: This decision was made because Accra had a drier climate relative to Cape Coast.

clues.text: In 1877, this city took the capital job from an older coast town. It has held the job of capital ever since that year.
clues.narrowing: Shrinks the list to coast capitals that took the job in 1877 and kept it.

source.quote: in 1877, at the end of the second Anglo-Asante War, Accra replaced Cape Coast as the capital of the British Gold Coast

clues.text: This city's name grew from an old word for ants. Tall red anthills dotted the land round about, full of busy soldier ants on the move.
clues.narrowing: Nearly decisive: one capital's name grew from a word for ants.

source.quote: The word Accra is derived from the Akan word Nkran meaning "ants", a reference to anthills seen in the countryside around Accra.

clues.text: The parliament of Ghana meets in this city. Its top court sits here too, and the land is run from here.
clues.narrowing: Confirms it: Ghana's parliament and its top court are based in this city.

source.quote: The Parliament, Supreme Court of Ghana, Black Star Square and the Bank of Ghana are located in Accra.

reveal.blurb: This coastal city became the capital of the British Gold Coast in 1877, and it kept the job when Ghana won its freedom. Its name grew from a word for ants, after the anthills round about it. Accra is the capital of Ghana.
